answer.rationale: Current situation shows dual pressure: competitor pricing threat to SMBs and degraded activation/onboarding metrics (6% and 4% QoQ declines). While memory_57 shows referral incentives work for established customers and memory_73 shows deep discounts drive trials, the referral path doesn't address new-customer onboarding friction, and aggressive pricing risks margin and positions us reactively. Memory_31 and memory_86 both document that simplifying onboarding lifts activation and completion in self-serve segments—directly addressing the 4% onboarding decline and 6% activation decline we're seeing now. Memory_91 suggests activation messaging also improved engagement. I'm verifying memory_31 and memory_91 to confirm the durability and magnitude of those gains and whether they compound. A small guarded test of simplified onboarding (fewer required fields at signup, streamlined first steps) on SMB cohorts addresses both the activation decay and positions us on quality of experience rather than price; it also preserves runway for a second experiment if results warrant pivot. This protects long-term qualified revenue by strengthening conversion and time-to-value rather than eroding unit economics.
